lead: LeRobot, from Hugging Face, puts data, policies, and commands for recording, training, and running in one place. In this lesson you train a real ACT policy for a few steps and end up with a checkpoint on disk. No robot and no account needed.
objetivo: install LeRobot 0.6, train a small policy, and understand the record → train → run cycle.

aprende.t: The record → train → eval → rollout cycle
Train an ACT in 200 steps and find the checkpoint
Read the loss in the log without fooling yourself
How long it takes on GPU and on CPU

hero_alt: A developer's desk with a laptop showing a training curve next to a small robotic arm and a USB camera.

secoes.sub: Four commands. The middle two don't need a robot. Click each one.

nos.detalhe: You teleoperate the arm and the command records cameras, joints, and actions in episodes. It needs the robot. Without a robot, use a public dataset from the Hub, like PushT from lesson 4.
The policy learns to imitate the actions in the dataset. You pick the type with --policy.type. This is the hands-on part of this lesson.
Puts the policy in a simulated environment and measures how often it succeeds. That's lesson 6.

New in 0.6 (Jul 2026). Runs the policy on the real arm. With the dagger strategy, you take over when it makes a mistake, and each correction is recorded with an intervention marker for the next fine-tuning.

secoes.volta: The rollout corrections come back as a dataset for the next training run
secoes.legenda: Recording and running need the arm. Training and evaluating run on any computer.
secoes.dica: ACT = Action Chunking with Transformers: a small policy that returns chunks of actions, the idea from lesson 2.

secoes.titulo: What you need to know before training

texto: Since 0.6, the base package is lean: to train, install lerobot[training]. For simulation, use extras like [pusht] or [aloha].
Python 3.12 and PyTorch 2.7 or newer. Some options were renamed: eval_freq became env_eval_freq, and --dataset.vcodec became --dataset.rgb_encoder.vcodec.
The 200 steps in this exercise took 26 s on an NVIDIA GPU (GB10) and 321 s, about 5 minutes, on just the 20-core CPU of the same machine (10/19/2026). A regular laptop will be slower.
Real training is a different scale: the LeRobot docs say training on your own robot takes several hours. The 0.6 hardware guide measures memory and time per policy family.
For this exercise, a CPU is enough. For long training runs, 0.6 supports the same lerobot-train in the cloud with --job.target, through HF Jobs, which is billed by usage and requires an account.
You don't need it for the course: everything here runs locally.
The SO-101 is LeRobot's entry-level arm. With the leader and follower pair, you record your own dataset with lerobot-record and train the same way.
LeLab runs the whole flow in the browser, with no command line, and today it only supports the SO-ARM101.

secoes.sub: Same venv as lesson 4. Swap cuda for cpu if you don't have an NVIDIA GPU.

blocos.rot: With the SO-101 (from the docs, needs the arm)
blocos.conteudo:
lerobot-record \
  --robot.type=so101_follower \
  --robot.port=<follower port> \
  --teleop.type=so101_leader \
  --teleop.port=<leader port> \
  --dataset.repo_id=<your username>/meu-dataset \
  --dataset.num_episodes=5 \
  --dataset.single_task="Pick up the black cube" \
  --dataset.streaming_encoding=true \
  --dataset.encoder_threads=2

LeRobot 0.6.1, NVIDIA GB10 GPU: 26 s total. CPU only: 321 s, final loss 3.536. Lines shortened with "...". The first time, it also downloads the ResNet-18 weights that ACT uses for vision.

• Forgetting --policy.push_to_hub=false: without it, training stops right at the start with ValueError: 'repo_id' argument missing. Please specify it to push the model to the hub. (tested on 10/19/2026): by default it wants to push the policy to the Hub.
  • Thinking low loss = good robot: the loss measures how well it imitates the dataset. The evaluation in lesson 6 tells you whether the policy works.
  • --policy.device=cuda without an NVIDIA GPU: swap it for cpu.

secoes.sub: About 5 minutes on CPU, under 1 minute on GPU.

exercicios.texto: Run the lerobot-train from the panel (with cpu or cuda). Time it.
In the log, find the step:50 and step:200 lines and write down both losses.
exercicios.pronto: the loss at step 200 is lower than at step 50, and you noted how long the training took on your machine.

exercicios.titulo: E3 · More steps (optional, with a GPU)
exercicios.texto: Repeat with --steps=5000 --save_freq=5000 --batch_size=32 and a different --output_dir. Keep the checkpoint: lesson 6 compares the two.
exercicios.pronto: the checkpoints/005000 folder exists (here it took 474 s on the GPU, with a final loss of 0.329).

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Which commands in the cycle run without a robot?
perguntas.explica: Training uses a dataset (it can come from the Hub) and evaluating uses simulation. Recording and rolling out need the arm.

perguntas.p: Where is the checkpoint after training?
perguntas.explica: With --output_dir=outputs/train/act_pusht_teste, the checkpoints go in checkpoints/000200 and checkpoints/last. With push_to_hub=false, nothing is uploaded.

perguntas.p: The loss dropped from 14.6 to 3.5. What does that guarantee?
opcoes: That the policy gets the task right.
That it imitates the dataset better; whether it gets the task right, only evaluation tells.
That it can go to the real robot.
perguntas.explica: Loss measures the imitation error on the training data. In lesson 6 you see that 200 steps still give 0% success on PushT.

perguntas.p: What is the dagger strategy in lerobot-rollout for?
opcoes: To train faster on the GPU.
So you take over the arm when the policy makes a mistake and record the correction as new data.
To upload the model to the Hub.
perguntas.explica: Run, correct, and fine-tune again: the corrections are tagged with intervention and go into the next training run. This is the link to lesson 7.

itens.texto: record, train, eval, rollout. Train and eval don't need a robot.
lerobot[training], Python 3.12, push_to_hub=false to train without an account.
200 steps: 26 s on GPU, 5 min on CPU here. Real training: hours.
